description: Use when a manufacturer of hardware or software sold in the EU learns of an actively exploited vulnerability or a security incident in its product. Applies Art. 14 of the Cyber Resilience Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/2847), in force since 11 September 2026: whether a report is due, the 24-hour, 72-hour and final report deadlines, where to report, and informing users.

affects_data_or_functions_protection.description: Severe incident test, Art. 14(5)(a): it harms or can harm the product's ability to protect the availability, authenticity, integrity or confidentiality of sensitive or important data or functions

event.description: actively_exploited_vulnerability: reliable evidence that a malicious actor exploited it; severe_incident: an incident affecting the product's security

is_manufacturer.description: Develops or manufactures the product, or has it designed or made, and markets it under its own name or trademark

malicious_code.description: Severe incident test, Art. 14(5)(b): it led or can lead to malicious code in the product or in users' systems

product_with_digital_elements.description: Software or hardware product (and its remote data processing) made available in the EU whose intended or foreseeable use includes a data connection to a device or network (Arts. 2(1), 3(1)); some products under sector laws, such as medical devices and vehicles, are excluded (Art. 2(2)-(4))

name: cra_reporting_check
title: Cyber Resilience Act: must the manufacturer report?
